input.question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".
input.ground_truth: It isn't just "goat cheese", it's just that your average American doesn't have enough experiences with goat cheeses to name any particular one. Feta, Kunik, Castelo Branco, and Clochette are all (at least partially) goat cheese that I've eaten personally. I'd think that pretty much everyone in the US has some experience with feta at a minimum.

Question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".

response.prediction:
Okay! Let's imagine cheese is like ice cream.

When you make ice cream from cow's milk, people make lots and lots of different flavors—like chocolate, strawberry, cookie dough, and more! That's because cow's milk is very common and people have made ice cream (or cheese) from it for a very long time. So, they tried many ways to make it taste different, and now there are lots of kinds.

But when you make ice cream from goat's milk, it tastes a little different all by itself. People usually just call it "goat milk ice cream" (or "goat cheese") because that's how it tastes and smells. Not as many people make cheese from goat's milk, and it doesn't change as easily, so we mostly just call it "goat cheese."

So, there are many kinds of cow cheese because people have tried lots of ways to make it taste different. But goat cheese mostly just tastes like goat, so we just call it "goat cheese."
